recipes.name: Real Italian Calzones
ingredients_raw: 2.5 cups all-purpose flour, plus more for dusting

steps.text: Make dough: Dissolve yeast in warm water in a mixing bowl; let sit until foamy, about 5 minutes. Add 1 tablespoon oil, sugar, and salt; mix in 1 cup flour until smooth. Gradually stir in remaining flour until dough is smooth and workable.

Turn dough out onto a lightly floured surface. Knead dough until it is elastic, about 5 minutes. Place 1 teaspoon olive oil in a large bowl; lay dough in the bowl and flip to coat with oil. Cover and let rise until almost doubled in size, about 40 minutes.
Meanwhile, make the filling: Combine Cheddar cheese, ricotta cheese, pepperoni, mushrooms, and basil leaves in a medium bowl. Mix well, cover, and refrigerate to chill.
Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Grease a baking sheet.
Punch down dough; divide into 2 equal pieces. Roll each piece out on a lightly floured surface into 1/8-inch-thick circles. Fill each circle with 1/2 of the cheese and meat filling.
Fold dough over filling to make a semicircle. Press edges down with the tines of a fork to seal. Brush the top of each calzone with beaten egg and place on the prepared baking sheet.
Bake in the preheated oven until golden brown, about 30 minutes. Serve hot.

raw_recipe.headline: Real Italian Calzones
raw_recipe.description: Calzones are easier to make than you think with homemade pizza dough stuffed with cheese, pepperoni, and mushrooms, baked until golden brown and hot.

video.description: Take your Italian dinner night to the next level by trying this decadent dish. In this video, join Nicole as she shows you how to make real Italian calzones with homemade dough. This baked recipe uses a delicious blend of ricotta, mozzarella, and Italian cheese melted together with pepperoni and basil to give these calzones an outstanding filling in the middle. After kneading and rolling out the dough, seal the filling and bake it in the oven.

review.reviewBody: This was a good recipe. It does need a few adjustments. The recipe should state that the yeast should proof first. I dissolved the sugar in the water with the yeast and let it sit for ten minutes. I didn't use the same toppings, I used ground ham, spinach, a little mozarella, mushrooms and of course ricotta, which makes a "real Italian Calzone, and for a little extra yum, a dash or two of Italian dressing, but the dough was great for calzone. Very chewy and beautiful coloring. I made 4 calzones out of this but cut them in half, so next time I will make 8 small ones. Also it took only 20 minutes when I used my pizza stone, so time should be adjusted for the size of individual servings.
I absolutely love these, I make 'em every week. Instead of egg I brush the dough with olive oil, to me it makes a better crust for a calzone. I also use Mozzerella instead of Chedder.

Excellent recipe. Very easy if you let your bread machine do the work. I set mine on dough cycle thru 2nd rise. Instead of Cheddar, I use a blend of Mozzarella and Romano, add green onions and black olives. Yummy! Thanks for sharing this great recipe, Jenny. It has become a favorite of my friends and family!

Made it similar to the recipe although this one screams to be made with whatever fillings you like. Like her tutorial, I used whole milk mozzarella and added a bit of provolone for some tang and stretchiness. No cheddar. I'm not sure why one would use cheddar in an Italian recipe like this one. I added spicy sausage and olives. I used the dough recipe as well and just mixed it on the dough setting in my bread machine. It turned out great! I made 2 like the recipe says and sent an un-baked one over to my neighbor. I hope they enjoy like I did...

I agree with mrsdi . I grew up in NY, and my mom was 100% Italian. We used to buy them pre-made at our Italian Deli and they only had Ricotta mixed with an egg, maybe some pepperoni or sausage, and could be served with sauce on the side if you wanted sauce on them. I echo Mrsdi "ONLY PURE RICOTTA CHEESE! Use one and one half cups of ricotta mixed with dash of pepper, salt, Italian sausage (or pepperoni is acceptable), one egg and dash of parsley and grated parmesan cheese." People who claim Calzone is just a pizza folded over are wrong too. The stuffing is primarily Ricotta---the real stuff, not cottage cheese.

This was my first attempt at homemade calzones, it was by request for my sons 18th birthday. I used a bread machine for the dough which came out perfect! I added a bit of italian seasoning and garlic salt to the dough which was a plus. Also I omitted the cheddar and replaced it with fresh grated mozzarella. We used black olives and marinated cherry tomatoes for the "toppings". Overall it came out great, the only issue I had was that the first one I assembled was ruined, probably because I rolled the dough out too thin. I chalked it up to a learning experience, and the other three came out perfect! I would highly recommend this recipe and will be making it again soon!

The dough is perfection-- soft but bakes with a moderate exterior crispness. However, the filling is too dry and bland for me. I like sauce inside as it picks up the flavors of the other ingredients. I used a very thin layer of ricotta/basil on the bottom, then did a light layer of sauce, and then topped it with chopped canadian bacon, kalamata olive and onion. I topped that with shredded mozarella and parmesan and brushed the top crust with olive oil. It was fantastic. Even if those fillings aren't to your taste, in the original recipe, rather than cheddar, I would try a great italian cheese- fontina, for example, mixed with fresh mozarella and some parmesan.

This recipe is awesome! The dough recipe is perfect and light; not thick, heavy and bready. I made the dough in my bread machine. Just follow bread machine standard by placing all wet ingredients in first then dry. I poked vents in the top of the calzones to let out the moisture from the mushrooms and brushed the top with olive oil and added some Sicilian blend seasoning I had on hand.

While I love making this recipe, I made the adjustment of not adding regular cheese and just using ricotta as per one reviewers comment. I've only made it that way and it's a family favourite. I have just figured out that if I pan fry the mushrooms first, they release all their moisture before baking and don't make the bottoms all soggy.

Made this Fantastic recipe many times now. I double the dough recipe and make two with the filling suggested and make two in a meat version. My meat version is 1lb hamburger, 1/2 pound mild or sweet sausage, 1/2 yellow onion. Cook meat and onion together and then add 1 cup spaghetti sauce. and salt to taste. Simmer for a few minutes. This is for people who can't have cheese!

The dough for the calzones was so easy to make and delicious. I used quick rise yeast and let the sugar, yeast and water sit for a few minutes before adding the flour. I used mozzarella cheese instead of cheddar, omitted the pepperoni and added onions. So good!! Will definitely be making again with different fillings. Also next time I might consider making 4 smaller calzones instead of 2 larger ones.
Delicious and easy! 😉

These are amazing! I struggle working with dough so believe me when I tell you this is a VERY FORGIVING Recipe 😂 I’ve made adjustments along the way with the filling and I add garlic, rosemary and basil to the dough and tonight the grands are excited because they get to make their own individual calzones!

As family favorite calzones they're delicious and the only thing I would do that or I like to do is put seasoning in the flour mix before you mix it all up that's always good learning that it's a great recipe. Lynn Fabela from Kansas City Missouri 👋 👋😋☺️
Having the sauce on the side was perfect. I made my dough in a bread machine.
Great and straightforward way to make homemade calzones. Will try different fillings next time for more variety.
Love this authentic Italian Calzone recipe. So did my family! Definitely a "make again"dish.

Perfect, easy dough. Made filling exactly as written and it was great! I've since made it with all manner of things in my fridge: different cheeses, different proteins, different vegetables. Love, love this recipe!

Will try again for sure. I did a traditional Italian filling of pepperoni, sausage and cheese in one and a spinach/artichoke/cheese filling from another Calzone recipe and the family loved them both. They were very good although the crust did turn out a little "tough". I used the dough recipe offered but made the dough in the bread machine. Was the 5 minutes of kneading after the bread machine cycle is finished too much working of the dough?

Super easy, loved everything about it. Came home after working a 12 hour shift and made this for dinner, that's how easy and good it was. Thank you for sharing, this will be on the weekly menu rotation
